messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: inference-prod cluster in az1c experiencing 5xx spike. 10m avg 5xx ~18%. Auto-pager sent to oncall-sre@maria.

maria (oncall-sre): acked. I'm on it. grabbing logs and current routing state. any recent deploys?

vikram (sre): no deploys to inference in last 30m from CI. seeing a lot of socket econnreset in host logs around the runtime processes and a pattern of KV cache timeouts to redis-proxy-az1c. traceroutes show intermittent packetloss to local redis nodes.

maria (oncall-sre): copy. can someone run a quick curl against /health so we have a baseline?

jonah (platform): ran a quick smoke, reproduces.
```bash
curl -v https://inference.redwood/api/v1/predict -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"input":"hello"}'
# 502/503 stream, connection reset after initial handshake
```

emily (customer-success): flagging customer impact — ACME and TinyBeta are reporting 5xx errors in their dashboards, multiple tickets. CS is aware and triaging.

maria (oncall-sre): ok plan: 1) reduce az1c weight in traffic routing 2) raise DNS TTL to enable faster failover if needed 3) spin up warm instances in az1a/az1b or eu-west-2 depending on capacity 4) AWS support escalation for host NIC flaps. I'll coordinate.

vikram (sre): for (1) we can change internal routing via the router service:
```bash
rd-router set-weights --service inference-prod --weights az1c=0,az1a=50,az1b=50 --reason "evacuate az1c due to network econnreset"
```
that will gradually drain traffic off az1c. Have to watch cache-affinity though — stateful requests might need sticky-handling.

jonah (platform): if you prefer lb-level, I can adjust target-group weights:
```bash
aws elbv2 modify-listener --listener-arn arn:... --default-actions '[{"Type":"forward","ForwardConfig":{"TargetGroups":[{"TargetGroupArn":"tg-az1c","Weight":0},{"TargetGroupArn":"tg-az1a","Weight":50},{"TargetGroupArn":"tg-az1b","Weight":50}]}}]'
```
I'll wait for your go.

maria (oncall-sre): go for router weight change first (less blast), jonah stand by to alter LB if needed. Also lowering internal DNS TTL from 300 -> 30 secs to speed up client failover.

ops-bot: autoscaling: scale-up triggered for inference-dedicated-pool in az1a: +3 instances provisioning.

vikram (sre): note: some requests rely on prefix KV cache pinned to az1c — draining will cause cache misses and a spike in latency. we'll enable graceful fallbacks in runtime: reduce max-inflight concurrency for affected routes so we don't cascade.

maria (oncall-sre): doing stateful mitigation: setting routing override + cache policy change now.

maria (oncall-sre): applied rd-router weight change. currently shifting ~85% of new connections off az1c. monitoring 1m.

jonah (platform): LB unchanged. ready to cut if backend errors persist after weight shift.

emily (customer-success): posting to impacted customers: "We're seeing an infrastructure issue impacting requests from the US-west region. Our SRE team is actively failing over traffic; some requests may see transient errors while we complete the failover. We'll update in 30 minutes."

maria (oncall-sre): setting runtime config to degrade KV cache affinity: fallback_mode=read-through with local memcache for 10s.
```json
{"route":"/v1/predict","cache":{"mode":"read-through","fallback_ttl_s":10}}
```

vikram (sre): logs show host-level NIC RX/TX errors on 3 g5 instances in az1c between 1938501200 and 1938501300. I think NIC-level flaps are causing socket resets. I'm collecting tcpdump to hand to AWS.

aws-support-bot: Support case opened: case# 1234567890. Preliminary AWS findings: host NIC counters show retran/err; possible hypervisor-level network instability isolated to az1c racks. AWS will investigate host-level fabric.

maria (oncall-sre): good. continuing failover. lowering DNS TTL now.

jonah (platform): changed internal DNS TTL to 30s (propagated to internal resolvers).

maria (oncall-sre): once traffic is stable at new weights and error rate <1% for 10m, we'll mark mitigation success and begin controlled restart of affected instances in az1c (do not rejoin pool until AWS confirms host NIC stability).

ops-bot: autoscaler: new instances in az1a are healthy and joined TG.

emily (customer-success): update: ACME confirmed reduced errors after ~6 minutes, they're seeing success rates improve. :white_check_mark:

vikram (sre): monitoring KV cache miss rate — it's spiked x3 but tail latency within acceptable bounds after rate limiting. continuing tcpdump capture and saving to s3://incidents/1938501234/pcap.tar.gz for AWS.

maria (oncall-sre): documenting timeline in incident runbook. opening incident doc for postmortem. tagging teams.

aws-support-bot: AWS: we've identified repeated NIC resets on a subset of hosts in az1c; mitigation options: live-migrate instances away from affected hosts or schedule host maintenance. We'll provide next steps within 45m.

maria (oncall-sre): decision: keep az1c weight=0 until AWS confirms hosts stable. Do not drain and rejoin automatically. We'll keep warm capacity in other AZs for the rest of the day.

vikram (sre): note for postmortem: root cause likely transient host NIC hardware/flap causing socket econnreset and subsequent KV cache stalls that amplified application errors. Need improved detection and auto-evacuation on NIC error thresholds.

emily (customer-success): sending follow-up comms to customers with ETA and mitigations performed.

maria (oncall-sre): handing this to night oncall, alex, for continued monitoring and followups. main outstanding items for handoff:
- monitor error rate and TTL propagation
- coordinate with AWS on host remediation and confirm when az1c instances are safe to rejoin
- verify no regression in cache fallback behavior
- finalize incident doc and severity classification

alex (sre-night): took the handoff. thanks @maria. I'll keep watches and escalate if AWS doesn't provide host remediation plan in the next 45m.

maria (oncall-sre): thanks all. :bow: closing active paging loop for now. leaving the thread open for updates.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigation in place — traffic rerouted off az1c, CS notified, AWS escalated. Incident owner: maria. Handoff owner: alex.
